title: Automate review publication and landing
summary: Add deterministic CLI commands for publishing metadata, preparing a PR branch, and archiving a merged review.
rationale: The first experiment required manual branch reconstruction and artifact moves. Encoding the accepted sequence in scripts reduces ambiguity and makes lifecycle preconditions executable.

decisions.summary: Permit publication only as a commit whose changed paths are under .semantic-review.
decisions.rationale: The metadata commit remains outside the semantic stage chain while preserving a reviewable artifact alongside the implementation branch.

decisions.summary: PR branch preparation refuses to move an existing branch to a different commit.
decisions.rationale: Approval automation must not silently overwrite another review or published branch.

alternatives.approach: Document the sequence of git add, commit, branch, merge, and move commands without scripting it.
alternatives.reasonRejected: The first experiment showed that ordering mistakes can close the semantic stack or leave the next review unable to initialize.

failedAttempts.approach: Move the artifact to history and stage both source and destination with a normal git add -A.
failedAttempts.outcome: The local .semantic-review ignore pattern also matched the nested archived directory, so Git refused to add it.
failedAttempts.lesson: Archive staging must force-add the exact validated destination while using normal deletion staging for the active root.

validation.summary: Covers metadata-only publication, PR branch preparation without overwrite, and committed artifact archival.
